description: A real Singapore Airlines boarding pass (one-way SIN to LHR, a long-haul overnight flight) came back with a returnDate that shouldn't exist at all. Departing SIN 23:25 and landing LHR 05:55 crosses midnight, so the ticket prints two different calendar dates (02 Jan departure, 03 Jan arrival) for what is a single flight leg -- the same shape the unlabeled-date fallback expects for a genuine departure+return pair (see the JNB<->CPT fixture), so it wrongly assigned the arrival day as returnDate. What actually distinguishes a same-leg overnight arrival from a real round trip: a real round trip's return leg reverses the route in its own text (the JNB<->CPT fixture's return leg literally says "Cape Town (CPT) to Johannesburg (JNB)"), while this ticket only ever mentions the SIN->LHR direction once; and this leg's destination (LHR) has a same-line local time earlier in the day than its origin (SIN) -- exactly what crossing midnight means, whereas JNB<->CPT's two legs each keep their own times within one day and aren't recorded as code-adjacent times at all. Fixed by requiring all three signals together before suppressing returnDate: the two dates are exactly one day apart, and both the resolved origin and destination have a recorded same-line time, and the destination's time is earlier than the origin's.
